ideas.title: My first motor boat (the drum motor now starts by itself)
ideas.critique: This is the first post where the motor carries something, and a tracking camera on a moving raft breaks the island's long run of fixed cameras watching objects move alone. The weakness is the water: still water with hand-made buoyancy is a rig for one setup, and blade drag against a water speed taken as zero is a plain formula, so the curving under a leaning friend has to really come out of the trim or it reads as scripted.

ideas.title: A merry-go-round the friends ride until it stalls
ideas.critique: Having the friends themselves be the load, choosing to get on and getting flung off, is a strong idea and the kind of creature interaction the human asked for. A merry-go-round is still a fairground prop people will expect, and a single turntable axis is a narrow rig. A torque-speed curve you can watch through riders getting on and off is the real gain.

ideas.title: Turn the ring on the axle until it sings
ideas.critique: Hearing a hum made from the real torque ripple and finding a sweet spot by hand is honest tinkering, and it is the first thing on the motor the player gets to adjust. It is still a bench knob on the same motor that has already had two posts, and once you have found the sweet spot there is little reason to turn it again.

ideas.title: Clam cells: bigger plates, faster motor
ideas.nearest: A wire that spins by itself
ideas.critique: This is the cart's power source, and the bank is a real puzzle with an answer to find, but a row of shells and a faster rotor make a picture people will see coming. Resistance as a conductivity-times-geometry formula plus a slow polarisation term is a modest model, and it holds only if it stays general across metals and brines.

ideas.title: The motor hauls its own stone up the cairn
ideas.critique: Going from stall to slip to generating, with the same circuit lighting a wire as the load falls back, is a reversal people will clip, and it reuses the solvers instead of a rig. The glowing wire repeats the last post's payoff, and the cairn event reads as an excuse more than as play.

ideas.title: Two carved gears for the hill
ideas.nearest: A copper wire keeps its bends
ideas.critique: Teeth that push each other through contact, with no ratio formula, is real engineering that generalises to any carving, and gear choice is a true design decision. It leans on a wheel-on-dune scene that does not exist yet, so its first step risks being two gears turning on a bench, which is nice to watch but small.

ideas.title: A wheel that drives itself across the sand
ideas.nearest: A snowball that grows as it rolls, a take that misses
ideas.critique: Bekker-Janosi terramechanics with ruts that stay is physics the island lacks and the hardest part of the cart, and it would hold up for any rim or slope. Seen from outside, though, it is once more one machine left alone on the ground while the camera watches, the island's most worn form, and a snowball has already left a stripe on its way downhill.

ideas.title: A fan on a sand yacht
ideas.critique: Blade-element thrust from a carved blade has many funny ways to fail, and a friend's hat blowing off is real play. A propeller cart sidesteps the cart's actual rolling problem, and the wake pushing leaves is likely to be a cosmetic force field rather than an air simulation.

ideas.title: Night machine: the commutator's sparks light the workshop
ideas.critique: Sparks sized by the real stored energy, lighting faces, show off the path tracer, and Archard wear is a real mechanism. It is still a device left running for a fixed camera to film, and a glowing object lighting its surroundings has already been posted; there is nothing for the player to do.

ideas.title: The friends' tug of war with the motor
ideas.critique: A friend pulling against the machine, calling for help and getting dragged off laughing, is the most social of the motor ideas and something people would replay. The Hill-muscle friends are new animation work that can easily fall back to sliding toys, and a rope on a stake moves the cart itself forward very little.
